proofs.text: Write the data file and read the bytes back; verify the text starts `const PURLIN_DATA = ` and ends `;` followed by a newline, and that reading the payload back returns the same commit sha the payload was built with

rule_text: The dashboard's data file is written as `const PURLIN_DATA = ` followed by the payload and a trailing semicolon, and reads back as the payload that was written

tests.body:
def test_the_data_file_is_a_const_assignment_and_round_trips(self, project):
        data = project.payload()
        path = purlin_payload.write_report_data(project.root, data)
        with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as handle:
            text = handle.read()
        assert text.startswith('const PURLIN_DATA = ') and text.endswith(';\n')
        assert purlin_payload.read_report_payload(project.root)['commit'] == (
            data['commit'])
